findings.summary: Rust fixed_system_path in environment.rs is defined pub(crate) but has no call site; the daemon environment block validator rejects PATH by name, so the function cannot be wired without a dedicated ProcessSpec field or bypass

fixedSystemPath returns null when SystemRoot and windir are both absent, and the exec caller silently proceeds without PATH — the exact failure mode the feature was introduced to fix; ensureSystemPath: true should fail explicitly rather than silently degrade

fixedSystemPath in system.ts does not validate that SystemRoot/windir is absolute and non-UNC before composing PATH entries; resolveBoundPowerShell in the same file applies isAbsolute and isUnc guards to the same variable — the inconsistency could produce a PATH containing a UNC or relative entry
const env changed to let env introduces a reassignment pattern; a single-expression computation would eliminate the let and make the implicit scrub-when-ensureSystemPath-is-true visible
Neither fixedSystemPath (TypeScript) nor fixed_system_path (Rust) has a unit test; interesting cases include both vars absent, trailing slashes, and the correct separator
Scrub-then-PATH ordering in exec is correct but untested; a future edit could silently reverse the order without breaking any existing test

LOCALAPPDATA exposure to the daemon is architecturally justified, but no test mechanically asserts that the daemon child environment cannot reach the governed project directory through the state base path
SystemRoot as a PATH entry includes the Windows root directory which is user-accessible on some configurations; not exploitable on a standard Windows installation
